title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 13
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: In a survey, 45 of 180 people said yes. A further 20 people are asked and all say yes. What percentage now say yes?
questions.explanation: Both figures move: 45 + 20 = 65 yes answers out of 180 + 20 = 200 people, which is 32.5%. Adding the new answers to the old total without enlarging the base gives 36.11%.

questions.prompt: The formula C = 5(F − 32) / 9 converts temperatures. What is F when C = 35?
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 9: 9 × 35 = 5(F − 32), so 5(F − 32) = 315 and F − 32 = 63. Adding 32 gives F = 95. Multiplying by 5 and dividing by 9 reverses the formula the wrong way and gives 51.44.

questions.prompt: Five numbers have a mean of 12 and a range of 10. The smallest is 7. What is the largest?
questions.explanation: The range is the largest minus the smallest, so the largest is 7 + 10 = 17. The mean of 12 is consistent with this — the five could be 7, 10, 11, 15, 17, totalling 60 — but it is not needed to answer the question.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, a shape is a 14 cm by 9 cm rectangle with a semicircle drawn on one 14 cm side, replacing it. What is the perimeter of the shape?
questions.explanation: The outline runs up one side, along the far 14 cm side, down the other side, then round the semicircle: 9 + 14 + 9 + 22 = 54 cm. The arc is half the circumference of a circle of diameter 14: 22/7 × 14 ÷ 2 = 22 cm. Treating it as an ordinary rectangle gives 46 cm, and adding the whole circumference rather than half of it gives 76 cm.

questions.prompt: A journey of 300 km is driven at 80 km/h, with a 25-minute stop along the way. How long does the whole journey take?
questions.explanation: Driving takes 300 / 80 = 3.75 hours, which is 225 minutes, or 3 hours 45 minutes. Adding the 25-minute stop gives 250 minutes: 4 hours 10 minutes.

questions.prompt: Two numbers have a highest common factor of 12 and a lowest common multiple of 180. One of the numbers is 36. What is the other?
questions.explanation: For any two numbers, the product of the highest common factor and the lowest common multiple equals the product of the numbers themselves: 12 × 180 = 2,160. Dividing by 36 gives 60. Checking: the factor pair 36 and 60 does have HCF 12 and LCM 180.

questions.prompt: A committee of 2 is chosen at random from 5 men and 4 women. What is the probability that at least one woman is chosen?
questions.explanation: Count the committees with no women: 5 men give 10 possible pairs, out of 36 pairs in all. So the chance of no woman is 10/36, and the chance of at least one is 1 − 10/36 = 26/36, which cancels to 13/18. Counting the "at least one" cases directly means adding two separate cases and is easy to get wrong.

questions.prompt: An item costing £45.00 is marked at £72.00 and then sold with 25% off the marked price. What is the profit as a percentage of cost?
questions.explanation: The discount brings the price to £54.00, a profit of £9.00 on a cost of £45.00 — 20%. Selling at the marked price would have made 60%, which is the figure to beware of.

questions.prompt: The sum of 3 consecutive multiples of 7 is 210. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: With three terms evenly spaced, the middle one is the mean: 210 / 3 = 70. The three are 63, 70 and 77, so the largest is 77. 70 is the middle term.

questions.prompt: A tap delivers 18 litres a minute. How long do 2 such taps take to fill a tank holding 4,050 litres?
questions.explanation: 2 taps deliver 36 litres a minute, so the tank takes 4,050 / 36 = 112.5 minutes, or one hour and 52.5 minutes. One tap alone would take 225 minutes; dividing the rate by the number of taps instead of multiplying gives 450 minutes.

questions.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is 115 degrees, and one of the two interior angles opposite it is 48 degrees. What is the other opposite interior angle?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles opposite it, so the other is 115 − 48 = 67 degrees. 65 degrees is the interior angle next to the exterior one, which is a different angle in the same diagram.

questions.prompt: Thirty scores are recorded: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears 7 times, 3 appears 5 times, 4 appears 9 times, 5 appears 6 times. What is the median?
questions.explanation: With 30 values the median sits between the 15th and 16th. Running totals are 1: 3, 2: 10, 3: 15, 4: 24, 5: 30, so the 15th value is 3 and the 16th is 4, giving a median of 3.5. The most frequent score, 4, is the mode, not the median.

questions.prompt: A jacket sells for £68.00 after a 15% discount. What was the price before the discount?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 85% of the original, so the original is £68.00 / 0.85 = £80.00. Adding 15% to the sale price gives £78.20, because 15% of the smaller figure is less than 15% of the larger one.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest number that must be added to 5,437 to make it divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 9 when its digits add to a multiple of 9. The digits of 5,437 add to 19, and the next multiple of 9 above that is 27, so 8 must be added. 1 is the remainder, which is what must be taken away instead.

questions.prompt: A triangle has vertices at (0, 0), (6, 0) and (4, 5). What is its area?
questions.explanation: The side from (0, 0) to (6, 0) lies along the x-axis and is 6 long, and the third vertex is 5 above that line, so the height is 5. The area is 6 × 5 / 2 = 15. Forgetting to halve gives 30.

questions.prompt: A worker is paid £13.60 an hour for 38 hours and time and a half for 6 hours of overtime. What is the week's pay?
questions.explanation: The basic hours pay 38 × £13.60 = £516.80. Overtime pays £20.40 an hour for 6 hours: £122.40. Together that is £639.20. Paying all 44 hours at the basic rate gives £598.40.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, what is f(-2)?
questions.explanation: Substituting: 2 × (-2)² = 2 × 4 = 8; −3 × (-2) = +6; and the constant is 1. Adding gives 15. Treating −3x as −6 rather than +6, by forgetting that x is negative, gives 3.

questions.prompt: 3 litres of a 20% solution are mixed with 5 litres of a 36% solution. What is the strength of the mixture?
questions.explanation: The two lots hold 0.6 and 1.8 litres of the active ingredient, 2.4 litres in 8 litres of mixture: 30%. Averaging the two strengths gives 28% and ignores that there is more of the stronger solution.

questions.prompt: £12,000.00 rises by 30% in one year and then falls by 20% the next. What is it worth at the end?
questions.explanation: After the rise it is £15,600.00, and 20% of that is £3,120.00, leaving £12,480.00. Netting the percentages to a 10% gain gives £13,200.00, because the fall is taken from the larger figure.

questions.prompt: Two similar jugs have heights in the ratio 4 : 7. The smaller holds 320 ml. How much does the larger hold?
questions.explanation: Volumes of similar solids scale as the cube of the length ratio: 7³ / 4³ = 343 / 64. So the larger holds 320 × 343 / 64 = 1,715 ml. Scaling by the heights themselves gives 560 ml and treats volume as if it had one dimension.

questions.prompt: A module is marked 40% on coursework and 60% on an exam. A student scores 72 on the coursework and 58 on the exam. What is the final mark?
questions.explanation: Weight each score by its share: 0.4 × 72 = 28.8 and 0.6 × 58 = 34.8, giving 63.6. Averaging the two scores gives 65 and treats the exam as if it counted the same as the coursework.
